newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 9.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- CELLNET TO BUY 40 PERCENT STAKE IN DIXONS LINK CHAIN

UK cellular phone group Cellnet is set to pay 25 million stg for a 40 percent stake in The Link, the Dixons Group's consumer electronics chain that specialises in fixed and mobile phones, pagers and personal organisers. Dixons has called the deal "fabulous" and Cellnet will pay a further 32 million stg over five years.
-- BOYCOTT FORCES HOECHST TO DROP ABORTION PILL

German pharmaceutical company Hoechst has been forced to end involvement with RU 486, the controversial abortion pill, after US abortion activists announced a boycott of its products. Hoechst's French subsidiary has said it could not risk continuing to produce the drug, which is sold in Britain, France and Sweden. It is the first instance of a company giving up its rights to a drug deemed safe and effective.
-- SUMITOMO DIRECTORS FACE SUIT OVER LOSSES OF $2.6 BILLION

Shareholders in the Japanese company Sumitomo have decided to sue the company's management because the company lost $2.6 billion in a copper trading scandal last year. It is the first time Japanese directors had been sued for failing to provide proper management controls and is a landmark case for a country known for shareholder passivity. Sumitomo has declined comment.
-- PENSION FUND RETURNS SHOW SHARP FALL

Returns from UK pension funds fell by almost 50 percent last year, according to a report by statistical company Combined Actuarial Peformance Services. The decline reflected poorer performances by security markets in 1996, and the downturn will increase costs for employers who run final salary pension schemes. Research also shows many investment managers failed to beat targets set by the trustees who govern pension funds.
-- MATURE MOBILE PHONE MARKETS RINGS THE CHANGES

UK telecommunications firm Cellnet's acquisition of a significant stake in The Link indicates a shift in the mobile phone industry from service providers towards retailers and High Street. Customer care is becoming very important in gaining and keeping subscribers. Questions are raised about the future for service providers with no financial connection to network operators. The Financial Times' Alan Cane said if independent service providers are to hold off large vertically integrated groups, tough rules and regulations are needed from telecoms watchdog Don Cuickshank.
-- REGULATOR PRESSES POWER SUPPLIER OVER JOINT VENTURE

The regulator has asked Privatised power distribution and transmission company Northern Ireland Electricity to clarify reports it is hopes to earn unregulated profits by contracting out billing and accounting services to a joint venture with United Utilities-owned Vertex Data Science, a financial services company. Ofreg will see links with Vertex do not "prejudice the consumer" and consumers and not shareholders benefit from the savings. Union officials have said the reports may cost jobs.
-- IBC AIDED BY STRONG TELECOMS MARKET GROWTH

The IBC group increased pre-tax profits by 10 percent to 13.7 million stg in 1996 due to the continuing popularity of conferences and exhibitions. IBC increased sales 24 percent to 120.3 million stg, including newsletter and magazine publishing, electronic media and training courses. Operating profits in IT and Telecoms doubled to 3.3 million stg. Chief executive Peter Rigby said the performance had been underpinned by 'explosive' growth in the telecoms market.
-- EU LEVY HITS GOLDEN VALE

Irish dairy Golden Vale has reported 6.3 million Irish pounds (6 million stg) pre-tax profits for 1996 compared to 16.5 million Irish pounds in 1995. The drop was due to weak milk product prices and a four million Irish pounds fine related to the quotas from the EU. The company has been without a chief executive director for six months because of the EU levy resulting from the company exceeding its milk quota in 1996.
-- ENERSIS UNITS PLAN 4.2 BILLION DOLLAR INVESTMENT

Over the next five years, subsidiaries of US utility-based Enersis plan to invest $2.5 billion in domestic operations and $1.7 billion in Argentina, Brazil and Peru. Chief executive Jose Yuraszeck did not mention the possibility of the group investing in future privatisations within the region.

-- MOTOROLA PREDICTS 'VERY GRADUAL' SEMICONDUCTOR RECOVERY The US communications, electronics and semiconductor group Motorola has predicted the worldwide semiconductor industry will increase by 10 percent in 1997 as opposed to the 'very gradual' growth of the industry in 1996. On Monday, the group announced a five percent decrease in sales by the semiconductor business in the first quarter from $7 billion to $6.6 billion. The group does not expect a double digit increase in sales because of continuing pricing pressures.
